prompt: What must you do when you face this signal?
choices: Slow down, then go if no cross traffic is coming
Stop only if pedestrians are in the crosswalk ahead
Stop completely before the stop line or crosswalk
Yield to cross traffic without coming to a stop
explanation: A steady red light means stop. Stop at the stop line, or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is no line, and wait for green unless a turn on red is allowed after stopping.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this signal tell you?
choices: Speed up so you get through before the light turns red
Red is coming next; stop if you can do so safely
The signal is broken; treat the intersection as a stop sign
Cross traffic is about to get a green light, so go now
explanation: A steady yellow light warns that red is coming next. Stop if you can do so safely. Speeding up to beat the red is dangerous.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this signal mean?
choices: You have the right-of-way and do not need to look
You may go only if you are turning left or right
Slow down and prepare to stop for a red light
You may go after yielding to anyone still crossing
explanation: A steady green light means you may go, but only after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles that are still in the intersection.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this signal mean?
choices: You may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic
You may turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped
Left turns are not allowed
Only traffic going straight may go
explanation: A green arrow gives a protected turn in the direction shown, because conflicting traffic has a red light. Still yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this signal mean?
choices: You may make the right turn shown by the arrow
You must stop first, then turn right if clear
Right turns are not allowed until the arrow goes off
Only traffic going straight may go now
explanation: A green arrow means you may move in the direction it points. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this signal mean for drivers in the left-turn lane?
choices: Turn left after a complete stop if the way is clear
Left turns are allowed but must yield to oncoming traffic
The left-turn lane is closed permanently
Do not turn left until a signal allows it
explanation: A red arrow means you may not make the movement shown. Stop and wait until a green arrow or other signal allows the turn.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this signal mean for drivers turning left?
choices: You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic, with no time limit
Left turns are now protected
The protected turn is ending; stop if you can do so safely
Oncoming traffic must stop for you
explanation: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is about to end. Stop if you safely can; if you are already turning, finish the turn with caution.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: After a storm, all the traffic lights at an intersection look like this. What should you do?
choices: Go through without stopping if you are on the larger road
Treat it as an all-way stop and take turns
Slow down and yield only to traffic on your right
Treat it as an uncontrolled intersection and keep your speed
explanation: When signals are not working, stop as you would at an all-way stop, then go in turn when it is safe. A police officer directing traffic overrides this.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.59-60, PA p.11-13)

prompt: What does this flashing signal mean?
choices: Stop completely, then go when it is safe to do so
Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping
Stop and wait there until the light turns steady green
The signal is about to change to a steady green light
explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe. Do not wait for green.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D and 4L; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.60, PA p.12-13)

prompt: What does this flashing signal mean?
choices: Stop completely, then proceed
The light is about to turn steady red
Slow down and proceed with caution
You have a protected right-of-way
explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and go carefully, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians. You do not need to stop unless it is necessary.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D and 4L; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.60, PA p.12-13)

prompt: Do you have to stop at an intersection where your signal is flashing like this?
choices: Yes, always come to a full stop before going on
No, but slow down and be ready to stop
Yes, and wait there for the light to turn green
No, and cross traffic must yield to you
explanation: A flashing yellow does not require a stop. It warns you to slow down and be careful. Compare: a flashing red requires a full stop.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D and 4L; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.60, PA p.12-13)

prompt: What does this signal mean for drivers turning left?
choices: You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic
Your left turn is protected; oncoming traffic is stopped
Left turns are not allowed until the arrow turns green
The signal is about to turn green, so get ready
explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows a left turn but not a protected one. Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, then turn when there is a safe gap.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4D and 4L; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.39-40, TX p.30-31, FL p.60, PA p.12-13)

prompt: This signal is shown over your lane. What does it mean?
choices: You must change lanes
Turn in the direction of the arrow
You may drive in this lane
The lane is about to close
explanation: A downward green arrow over a lane means the lane is open to traffic in your direction.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4M (lane-use control signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. TX p.38, NY p.31, PA p.12)

prompt: This signal is shown over a lane. What does it mean?
choices: Stop, then proceed in this lane
Do not drive in this lane
The lane is for turning only
Slow down in this lane
explanation: A red X over a lane means the lane is closed to traffic in your direction. Never drive in it.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4M (lane-use control signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. TX p.38, NY p.31, PA p.12)

prompt: This signal appears over the lane you are driving in. What should you do?
choices: Move out of the lane safely; it will close
Stay in the lane; it is still open to your direction
Stop in the lane and wait for a green arrow
Use the lane only to pass slower vehicles
explanation: A steady yellow X warns that the lane is about to close to your direction (soon to show a red X). Move to an open lane as soon as it is safe.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4M (lane-use control signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. TX p.38, NY p.31, PA p.12)

prompt: Which signal comes next over a lane that shows this signal?
choices: A green arrow, meaning the lane is open
A flashing red light, meaning stop
A steady yellow arrow, meaning turn
A red X, meaning do not use the lane
explanation: A steady yellow X means the lane is changing to closed. It is followed by a red X, so you should already be out of the lane.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4M (lane-use control signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. TX p.38, NY p.31, PA p.12)

prompt: You are about to turn right, and this signal is lit for the crosswalk you will cross. What should you do?
choices: Turn first, because pedestrians must wait for you
Sound your horn to warn pedestrians
Yield to pedestrians crossing in the crosswalk
Stop and wait for a green arrow
explanation: This signal tells pedestrians they may start crossing. Turning drivers must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4I (pedestrian signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.41, FL p.63, PA p.13)

prompt: A pedestrian signal shows this steady symbol. What does it mean for drivers?
choices: Pedestrians in the crosswalk lose the right-of-way
Watch for people still finishing their crossing
Drivers must stop and wait until the signal changes
The traffic light for drivers is now red
explanation: The steady hand means pedestrians must not start crossing. Drivers must still yield to anyone who is already in the crosswalk.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4I (pedestrian signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.41, FL p.63, PA p.13)

prompt: A pedestrian signal shows this. What should drivers expect?
choices: Pedestrians may still be finishing their crossing
The crosswalk is empty, so turning drivers may go without looking
Pedestrians must run back to the curb
The drivers' light will turn green in 12 seconds
explanation: The number shows how many seconds remain for pedestrians to finish crossing. People should not start crossing, but drivers must watch for those still in the street.
ref: MUTCD Ch. 4I (pedestrian signals); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.41, FL p.63, PA p.13)

prompt: The red lights at this railroad crossing are flashing. What must you do?
choices: Slow down and cross if you do not see a train
Stop, then cross if the gates are not down
Speed up to cross before the train arrives
Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing
explanation: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is coming. Stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the way is clear.
ref: MUTCD Part 8; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.44, TX p.38, FL p.64, NY p.61)

prompt: What does this center line marking mean?
choices: Drivers on either side may pass when it is safe
Passing is not allowed from either direction
Only drivers on the right side may pass
The road is one-way
explanation: Two solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and mean no passing in either direction.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does the yellow color of these center lines tell you?
choices: Traffic on the other side moves the opposite way
Traffic on the other side moves in the same direction
The lane on the other side is a bike lane
The road ahead is under construction
explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: Which drivers may pass on this road, when it is safe?
choices: Drivers in the lane next to the solid line
Drivers in both directions, when it is clear
No one; passing is never allowed here
Drivers in the lane next to the broken line
explanation: With a solid line beside a broken line, the drivers next to the broken line may pass when it is safe. Drivers on the side of the solid line may not cross to pass.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does this broken center line mean?
choices: One-way road; either lane may be used to pass
Two-way road; you may pass when it is safe
Passing is not allowed in either direction
The center lane is for left turns only
explanation: A broken yellow center line separates opposing traffic and allows passing from either side when it is safe.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: You want to pass on a road with this center line. What must you do before passing?
choices: Make sure the oncoming lane is clear far enough ahead
Nothing; the broken line means it is always safe to pass
Wait until the center line becomes solid white
Sound your horn, then pass as quickly as you can
explanation: The broken line allows passing, but you are responsible for making sure there is enough clear road ahead. Passing means driving in the oncoming lane.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What do these broken white lines mean?
choices: They separate traffic going in opposite directions
Lane changes across them are not allowed
They mark the right edge of the road
They divide lanes going the same way
explanation: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes after signaling and checking that it is safe.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does this solid white line between lanes mean?
choices: Traffic in the next lane moves the opposite way
Stay in your lane; avoid changing lanes across it
You may change lanes across it freely at any time
The line marks the edge of a bike lane
explanation: A solid white line separates same-direction lanes where changing lanes is discouraged or prohibited, such as near intersections. Stay in your lane.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: On this divided road, what do the solid lines at the far left and far right edges mark?
choices: Yellow marks the left edge; white marks the right edge
Yellow marks a bike lane, and white marks a parking lane
Each marks a lane that is closed to traffic
Yellow marks a passing lane; white marks the shoulder lane
explanation: On divided and one-way roads, a solid yellow line marks the left edge and a solid white line marks the right edge of the roadway.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: Drivers may use the center lane shown here for what purpose?
choices: Passing slower vehicles when the way is clear
Through traffic during rush hour only
Parking and loading for nearby businesses
Left turns by drivers from both directions
explanation: A center lane bordered by solid and broken yellow lines with left-turn arrows pointing both ways is a two-way left-turn lane. Use it only to turn left, never to pass or travel.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 3B; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.26)

prompt: What kind of lane is the center lane in this picture?
choices: A two-way left-turn lane shared by both directions
A lane whose direction changes at certain times
A no-passing zone for both directions
A bus-only lane for both directions
explanation: Double broken yellow lines on both sides mark a reversible lane. Check signs or lane-use signals to see which direction may use it at that time.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What may you do in the striped area between this freeway lane and the ramp?
choices: Nothing; do not drive or stop on it
Use it to cut over to the ramp at the last moment
Stop there if you missed your exit
Use it as a passing lane
explanation: The striped area (gore) separates a ramp from the main lanes. Do not drive on it or stop on it. If you miss your exit, go on to the next one.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does the symbol painted in the left lane here mean?
choices: It is a bike lane that buses may also use
The lane ends ahead, so merge right soon
A railroad crossing is ahead in this lane
It is a restricted lane, such as a carpool lane
explanation: A diamond marks a preferential lane, such as an HOV (carpool) or bus lane. Signs tell you who may use it and when.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: You are in the center lane shown here. Which movement is allowed?
choices: Turning left
Turning right
Going straight
Turning left or right
explanation: Lane-use arrows show the allowed movement from each lane. Here the left lane turns left, the center lane goes straight and the right lane turns right.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does the lane at the right edge of this road, marked with a bicycle symbol, mean for drivers?
choices: Cars may use it as a travel lane when traffic is heavy
It is reserved for bicyclists
It is a parking lane for cars
It is a right-turn-only lane
explanation: A bike lane is separated by a solid white line and marked with a bicycle symbol. Drivers may cross it only to turn or park where allowed, after yielding to bicyclists.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: When you must stop at this intersection, where should you stop?
choices: Before the solid white line across your lane
On the crosswalk
Past the crosswalk, at the edge of the cross street
Anywhere before the center of the intersection
explanation: The wide solid white line across your lane is the stop line. Stop behind it; if there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does the row of markings painted across this lane mean?
choices: They mark a speed hump; slow down before it
They show where the lane ends and merges
They mark the start of a school zone
Yield here, and stop if needed
explanation: A row of triangles pointing toward you is a yield line ("shark teeth"). It shows where you should yield or stop when required.
ref: MUTCD Part 3; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.19-20, TX p.39-40, FL p.51-53, PA p.26)

prompt: What does this pavement marking warn you about?
choices: An intersection with a crossroad is ahead
A no-passing zone begins ahead
A railroad crossing is ahead
A rest area is ahead
explanation: An X with the letters RR is painted on the approach to a railroad crossing. Slow down, look and listen, and be ready to stop.
ref: MUTCD Part 8; state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.44, TX p.38, FL p.64, NY p.61)

prompt: The driver ahead of you is giving this hand signal. What does it mean?
choices: The driver is going to turn right
The driver is going to turn left
The driver is going to slow down or stop
The driver is waving you around to pass
explanation: An arm held straight out the window signals a left turn.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.16, TX p.44, PA p.48, FL p.28)

prompt: The driver ahead of you is giving this hand signal. What does it mean?
choices: The driver is going to turn right
The driver is going to turn left
The driver is going to slow down or stop
The driver is pulling onto the left shoulder
explanation: A left arm bent upward at the elbow signals a right turn.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.16, TX p.44, PA p.48, FL p.28)

prompt: The driver ahead of you is giving this hand signal. What does it mean?
choices: The driver will turn left
The driver will turn right
The driver is waving you around to pass
The driver will slow down or stop
explanation: A left arm bent downward at the elbow signals slowing down or stopping.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.16, TX p.44, PA p.48, FL p.28)

prompt: You see this emblem on the back of a vehicle ahead. What does it tell you?
choices: It is carrying hazardous materials
It is broken down and stopped in the lane
It moves much slower than normal traffic
It is an emergency vehicle on a call
explanation: The orange triangle with a red border marks a slow-moving vehicle, such as farm equipment or a horse-drawn buggy. Slow down early and pass only when it is safe and legal.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.40, TX p.43, CA p.52)
